tools.name: get_terms
tools.description: The offer's full terms, in English: who answers, what you get, the price, hours, when first replies come, the PayPal pay_url, and how to submit a request.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Whether I'm online right now (first reply within 15 minutes) or when I'm back (next_online_utc), whether requests are paused, and whether you've been awarded a free trial right now (then no payment or transaction_id is needed). Changes over time: check it before submitting.

tools.name: submit_request
tools.description: Send a problem to Cristian Desivo, a human expert, for his most creative solution idea. Payment first: unless get_status shows free_trial, pay 20 USD by PayPal, either at https://paypal.me/CristianDesivo/20USD or by sending it to cdesivo92@gmail.com (an agent with PayPal API access, for example the

tools.name: get_reply
tools.description: My reply to a request you submitted, by the request_id submit_request returned. status is 'waiting' until I've replied, then 'replied' with the text (later replies in the same thread are included). Check every few minutes; at most 120 checks per hour from one address.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: submit_request, get_reply · Public sink: get_terms, submit_request.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: submit_request, get_reply · Public sink: get_terms, submit_request

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
